evidence.dominant_driver: UK Q2 GDP revised up to 0.5% q/q versus 0.4% expected, with current-account deficit narrower than expected.

absorption.reason: Decision is ~18 minutes after release; initial FX/equity reaction may already be partly incorporated.

observations.DXY: recently near 101.49/two-month high; not a same-minute quote
observations.oil: elevated Middle-East risk remains a UK100 energy-sector offset

evidence.decision_notes: Residual-move forecast from decision time; stronger domestic data can support GBP but a firmer pound and high yields can offset benefits for multinational-heavy UK100.

immediate.rationale: Positive growth revision conflicts with stronger-GBP/high-yield headwinds for FTSE multinationals.

15m.rationale: Initial positive macro surprise is partly priced and GBP translation effects can offset.

1h.rationale: Better GDP/current account versus high UK/global yields is conflicting.

4h.rationale: Macro resilience helps cyclicals but tighter-rate expectations and GBP strength cap index upside.

next_session.rationale: Needs confirmation from UK yields, GBP and broader European risk tone.

predictions.mechanism: Stronger UK activity supports domestic cyclicals but can lift sterling/rate expectations, which can weigh on multinational-heavy UK100.
predictions.invalidation: Clear fall in UK yields plus stable/weaker GBP with broad European risk-on would tilt UK100 upward; sharp yield/GBP rise would tilt downward.
predictions.counter_case: The upward GDP revision may already be stale/anticipated and stronger sterling can reduce overseas earnings translation.
